requirement: Safely purge workspace files, symlinks, and directories without traversing symlinks outside workspace root, preventing arbitrary deletion of external files.
skeleton: SafeWorkspaceCleaner class with clean_target method ensuring paths stay within workspace_root and unlinking symlinks without following them.
caption: A standard-library workspace cleaner built on pathlib and shutil that deletes only what lives inside its root and never follows a link out of it, with no third-party imports. SafeWorkspaceCleaner resolves workspace_root strictly at construction. clean_target(target_path) joins a relative path onto the root, keeps an absolute one as given, and resolves only the candidate's parent directory, returning False when that parent does not exist. It raises PermissionError unless the resolved parent equals the root or is_relative_to it, a path-component comparison rather than a string prefix, so a sibling directory whose name merely begins with the workspace name is refused. Before any resolution of the candidate itself it checks is_symlink and, for a link, calls unlink on the link and returns True, so the directory or file it points to is never touched. A missing candidate returns False, and a regular file is unlinked and returns True. For a real directory it resolves the full path, raises PermissionError when that resolved directory escapes the root, and otherwise removes it with shutil.rmtree and returns True. The fixture asserts removal of an ordinary file and subdirectory, that a link to an external directory is removed while the external important.txt keeps its CRITICAL DATA, that a directory containing a link outward is deleted without traversing it, that a parent escape is refused, that a sibling-prefix path is refused with the sibling's file intact, and that a directory symlink is unlinked cleanly.

rationale.teaches: Workspace cleanup that unlinks a symlink instead of following it, checks containment with is_relative_to on the resolved parent, and raises on escape.
rationale.why: rmtree on a directory symlink or a walk with followlinks deletes files outside the workspace, which no in-workspace test notices. The fixture plants a symlink to an external directory and checks the external files survive.

candidates.why_wrong: The candidate is resolved before the symlink check, so a symlink to an external directory is treated as that directory and its contents are deleted.
Containment is a string prefix check, so a sibling directory whose name starts with the workspace name is accepted.
The symlink check is missing, so a directory symlink is passed to rmtree and the target's files are removed.
The walk follows symlinks, so files reachable through a link outside the workspace are unlinked.
An escaping path returns False instead of raising PermissionError, so the caller cannot distinguish refusal from a missing target.
